questions.prompt: You must call $10 into a $40 pot. Break-even equity is about…
questions.explanation: Risk 10 to win 50 total after the call, so 10/50 = 20%. Or 10/(40+10).

questions.prompt: You have about 32% equity with a flush draw on the flop and the pot offers you 4 to 1. If you will see both cards…

choices.text: The price is better than 20% break-even, so a call can be fine before implied odds.
Pot odds ignore the number of outs.

questions.explanation: 4 to 1 is 20 percent. Thirty-two percent clears that price if the draw is clean and you see both cards.

questions.prompt: A bluff that risks $50 to win $50 needs to work…

choices.text: More than half the time if you never win when called.

questions.explanation: Risk 50 to win 50 is even money. With no showdown value you need folds more than half the time.

questions.prompt: Which statement about EV is right?

choices.text: A winning session proves every call was correct.
Losing a called bluff means the call was a mistake.
You should never call without the nuts.
A +EV call can still lose this particular hand.

questions.explanation: One result is not the decision. EV is the average over the chances.
